claim: A scratch root is swept only where the run that made it ends of its own accord, so every killed run leaves its roots behind, and this workstation now holds 96133 of them.

evidence:
`/var/tmp` holds 118197 entries, 96133 of them named `akasha-`, and `du -sh /var/tmp` answers 210G, counted 2026-09-15.

`file/disk/modules/scratching/scratching.module.code.ts` makes every root: `SCRATCH_AT` is `/var/tmp`, `rootFor` calls `mkdtempSync(join(SCRATCH_AT, prefix))` and pushes the root onto a list its closure holds, and `sweep` reads that list calling `rmSync`. Nothing else knows the paths. `keptAt`, which sits in `file/disk/test-fixtures/kept-scratch/kept-scratch.test-fixture.code.ts`, is the only caller that arms a sweep of its own, by `process.on("exit", kept.sweep)` the first time it is asked. A `Scratch` a caller made with `scratchWorld()` is swept only where that caller calls `sweep`.

Why a kill leaks. `process.on("exit")` runs on a normal end and on an explicit `process.exit`, and does not run on SIGKILL, so a run something kills leaves every root that run made. A processor ceiling kills. `spawning` in `check/modules/audit-serving/audit-serving.module.code.ts` asks `bytes` for the `cpuCeiling` a check states as its `auditCeiling`, and `bytes` in `code/spawning/modules/running/running.module.code.ts` spawns the watcher `watching` builds wherever the run got a control group of its own; that watcher writes `cgroup.kill` once the group passes the ceiling, which is SIGKILL to every process in the group. Where no group was made no watcher runs and the run finishes. That kill leaves little behind, because `spawning` sweeps its own root in a `finally` and `/var/tmp` holds one `akasha-audit-child-` root. What else kills is `command/modules/stopping`, which SIGKILLs a command past the seconds its own page states, and the ending of a seat scope, which takes every process under that scope at once.

What the leak is made of, counted 2026-09-15 by prefix with the six characters `mkdtemp` adds left off, over 218 prefixes: 57995 `akasha-indexed-`, 9706 `akasha-transport-log-`, 8647 `akasha-page-entry-landing-`, 6604 `akasha-landing-`, 6067 `akasha-page-entry-queue-`, 1477 `akasha-file-arguing-`, 1085 `akasha-web-app-`, 426 `akasha-asking-`, 220 `akasha-move-`. `akasha-indexed-` is made at `page/index/test-fixtures/fixture-world/fixture-world.test-fixture.code.ts:271` through `keptAt` and at :285 through a `scratchWorld()` a caller holds.

Not established. I did not measure how much of the 210G is akasha's rather than another program's, and I did not read whether any workstation service already sweeps `/var/tmp`. I did not test a killed run to watch a root survive; what I say about `process.on("exit")` is read from how the handler is armed rather than from a run I killed. I did not judge whether the mend is a sweeper, a sweep armed on a signal, or a scratch root inside one folder a command clears.
